records.name: Dispersion-normalized cross-sectional equity forecast (location-to-spread)
records.rejection_reason: Rejected after the preregistered 2004-2026 costed replay: gross and net mean returns were -21.04 and -33.13 bps per leg, the recent-era mean was -50.86 bps, zero of six neighboring specifications were positive, bootstrap P(mean <= 0) was 0.9855, and incremental portfolio Sharpe was -0.0785. Dispersion normalization underperformed the raw-location control by 41.19 bps per leg.

records.name: Fixed-spacing grid harvest on US liquid equity ETFs
records.rejection_reason: Rejected after the preregistered 2000-2026 costed replay over 5,763 deployments on 27 US equity ETFs: the grid returned -54.86 bps gross and -64.69 bps net per 252-session deployment against the source's own same-initial-exposure static control, one of six neighboring specifications was positive, bootstrap P(mean <= 0) clustered by anchor date was 0.9914, bad-day co-loss with the active book was 84.51 percent, and incremental portfolio Sharpe was -0.0707. The preregistered exposure-matched control appeared to vindicate the grid at +431.80 bps, but that control's weight is the window's own realised average and the grid sheds exposure into strength, so weight shortfall and window return correlate at +0.805 and the entire advantage decomposes into that hindsight term. A hindsight-free constant-weight control leaves +19.15 bps per deployment at bootstrap p = 0.2256, indistinguishable from zero. Any future volatility-harvesting or rebalancing-premium proposal must be measured against a hindsight-free constant-weight control, never against the realised-average exposure match.

records.name: Rolling sign-test calendar-month seasonal fade on US liquid ETFs
records.rejection_reason: Rejected after the preregistered 2008-2026 costed replay over 556 deployments on 31 US-listed ETFs: net mean -152.57 bps per one-month deployment (gross -142.83, median -156.69, hit rate 35.25 percent), recent eight-year era -214.13 bps, zero of six neighboring lookback and significance-bar specifications positive, bootstrap P(mean <= 0) clustered by instrument and calendar year 1.0000, and incremental portfolio Sharpe -0.1699 at every sizing scale tested. Seven of eight preregistered falsifiers fired; only F6 (book correlation -0.1356, bad-day co-loss 20.70 percent) did not. The mechanism is arithmetic and generalizes beyond this rule: at an eight-year window a 0.10 two-sided exact binomial bar admits only the 8-0, 0-8, 7-1 and 1-7 patterns, which on US equity ETFs fires bullish 515 times out of 556, so any fade of it is a systematic short of instrument-months whose own realised return averaged +169 bps. The mirror is not an edge either: following returns +136.53 bps, which is long equity drift rather than seasonal content, and the fade loses -43.82 bps against the preregistered period-matched drift control as well as absolutely. The finding worth reusing is that the rolling sign test is not a direction detector on this tape: bullish-detected cells returned +168.3 bps against +117.8 for their non-detected peers that month and bearish-detected cells returned +177.4 against +137.6, so the statistic selects instrument-months that outperform regardless of which way it reads them. The within-instrument sign permutation is nominally favourable at p = 0.0326 and changes nothing, because a roughly +20 bps selection component cannot rescue a -172 bps direction mix. Any future calendar-detection proposal on a drifting asset class must report its detected-direction mix and a period-matched drift control before its headline number is read. This refutes the transported rule on US-listed ETFs and says nothing about the source's own spot-FX finding (SSRN 7434881); the market was transported only because contracts.py requires asset_class LISTED_EQUITY.

records.name: Intermediate-term maximum-drawdown reversal on US large-cap single stocks
records.rejection_reason: Rejected after the preregistered 2002-2026 costed replay over 286 non-overlapping monthly deployments and 8,534 positions on 162 US large-cap single stocks. This is the first candidate in this pipeline whose RETURN gates all passed and which was killed on PORTFOLIO FIT and risk attribution alone, so the reason matters more than the verdict. The costed long-short spread was +52.94 bps per monthly deployment (gross +76.97, median +48.57, hit rate 53.50 percent, recent eight-year era +69.09, six of six neighbours positive, month-clustered bootstrap P(mean <= 0) = 0.0782), and it beat the preregistered cumulative-return control by +68.42 bps at paired bootstrap probability 0.0346, with the two rankings genuinely distinct at mean per-month Spearman -0.4417. Two preregistered falsifiers fired, both portfolio: F6 on bad-day co-loss of 72.48 percent against a 60 percent bar (book correlation was fine at 0.1738, so requiring BOTH legs of F6 is what caught this), and F7 on incremental portfolio Sharpe of -0.0437 against the book's 2.0015, negative at 0.25x, 1x, 4x and risk-comparable 5.23x scale with a scale-free marginal derivative of -0.0119, so not a sizing artifact. The deterministic email gate independently failed the same two checks (co-loss above 35 percent, incremental Sharpe below 0.05) and passed its other twelve. THE MECHANISM, which is the part that generalizes: a dollar-neutral sort is not a beta-neutral sort. Ranking on maximum drawdown puts the highest-beta names on the long side by construction -- long leg mean trailing volatility 42.50 percent and mean 252-session SPY beta 1.320 against the short leg's 21.44 percent and 0.655, a leg beta gap of +0.665 implying 49,887 dollars of net beta-dollar exposure, 6.65 percent of the 750,000 dollar configured account, on a book holding equal dollars long and short. Accruing the market return on that declared gap month by month accounts for +68.93 bps of the +52.94 bps spread, leaving a residual of -15.99 bps at bootstrap probability 0.6938; the recent era decomposes the same way at +64.00 beta-implied and +5.10 residual. The same adjustment applied to both sorts shrinks the advantage over the cumulative-return control from +68.42 to +17.33 bps at probability 0.2969, because that control's own leg beta gap is -0.0006, i.e. beta-neutral. The +17.33 figure is an IN-SAMPLE DIAGNOSTIC, not hindsight-free incremental edge, and it uses one benchmark with no size, value or low-volatility factor available in this repository, so it is a FLOOR on what a real risk model would remove. Corroborating the same story from three independent directions: the sleeve's daily returns correlate +0.49 with SPY, its four worst months all fell on down-market months, and its return is concentrated entirely in high-volatility tape (low and mid SPY-volatility thirds returned -15.16 and -37.19 bps per month, high third +211.89). The strategy made money in absolute terms; that is a separate statement from beating a risk-matched control and the two must not be conflated. Fragilities recorded rather than used to reject: naive monthly t only 1.41 on a 637 bps monthly standard deviation, 12-month block bootstrap 0.1116 rather than 0.0782, the preregistered 20 bps cost case +32.94 bps at probability 0.1908, near-static leg membership (AMD long in 241 of 286 months) making the effective sample well below 286 and the drop-one tests weaker than their arithmetic suggests, and N5 -- skipping six months instead of twelve -- being the STRONGEST neighbour at +81.17 bps, which contradicts a thesis that reversal needs a full year to decontaminate from momentum and is unexplained. INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION (a second agent re-derived the whole 286-month walk-forward from raw bars with its own code, importing nothing from the research script): net_mean_bps reproduced to a deviation of 0.0, deployed-month sets and per-month eligible and leg counts identical, decile membership identical ticker for ticker in six sampled months, zero anti-monotonicity failures, neighbours N4 and N6 reproduced to 0.0, and the rebuilt active-book stream matched to $5e-5. It confirmed F6 and F7 as ROBUST: bad-day co-loss ranges 69.75 to 81.67 across eleven defensible conventions and clears the 60 bar in every one, incremental Sharpe stays negative at every scale, and both still fire on a book stream rebuilt with the OVS ledger bug corrected (correlation 0.1670, co-loss 72.15, incremental Sharpe -0.0424). It also found two things the original write-up missed, both recorded in that artifact's CORRECTIONS.md. First, F8 is a calendar-YEAR test and its pass is NOT evidence against episode concentration: at MONTH level the top 3 of 286 months are 50.2 percent of total net contribution and the top 10 are 127 percent, so the other 276 months are net negative in aggregate, and dropping the single best month takes net_mean from 52.94 to 43.42. Second, F4's non-firing is fragile and arguably wrong: the preregistered month clustering degenerates to an iid resample because the cross-section is already aggregated, and the 12-month moving-block bootstrap gives 0.1116 in the artifact and 0.1187 independently, both ABOVE the 0.10 bar. It also refuted one FALSE sentence in the artifact's interpretive section (the claim that the four worst months were the four worst market months -- only one of four overlaps), which is corrected there and does not carry the beta conclusion. STANDING REQUIREMENT this leaves behind: any future cross-sectional long-short proposal on this book must report its LEG BETA GAP and a beta-accrual decomposition of the spread before its headline number is read, because dollar-neutral is not beta-neutral and any drawdown, volatility, distress or loser-minus-winner ranking will generate a large beta gap by construction; and bad-day co-loss must be read beside correlation rather than behind it, because a 0.17 average correlation coexisted with a 72 percent co-loss rate here. SCOPE: the universe is 162 mega- and large-capitalization names, the cheapest-to-arbitrage end of the cross-section and exactly where SSRN 7442431's own costly-to-arbitrage mechanism predicts the weakest premium. This result is evidence about the large-cap claim in that paper's robustness section and is NOT a refutation of its headline CRSP-wide decile finding, which this repository cannot test. Present-day instrument selection is disclosed and no direction or bound is asserted for its effect on the strategy-minus-control result.
